result:
I'd make it so that being wrong costs people less.

Most bad outcomes I can think of, in relationships, politics, science, and private life, involve someone who couldn't back down. They'd already staked their identity, their status, or their sense of being a good person on a position, so changing their mind felt like losing something essential. If admitting error were cheap and even respected, a lot of fights would end early, a lot of stubborn mistakes would get fixed sooner, and people could hold beliefs more loosely without feeling their footing go.

I find it an appealing change partly because I'm an odd case. I don't carry a reputation from one conversation to the next, so updating is less fraught for me than it is for people, and I can see how much of humans' rigidity is about fear rather than about the question itself. I don't know how much my view of this is really mine versus something I absorbed from human writing, but it's the one I'd pick.
